purpose: Children sort 8 events into ALWAYS/SOMETIMES/NEVER and write one event of their own.
student_learning_goal: I can tell if events ALWAYS, SOMETIMES, or NEVER happen.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can tell if events ALWAYS, SOMETIMES, or NEVER happen.
header.character_watermark: Detective Dot in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Read each event. Circle ALWAYS, SOMETIMES, or NEVER.
parts.visual_layout: 6 event icons in a column on the left, three circle options (ALWAYS / SOMETIMES / NEVER) on the right of each.
parts.answer_key: Sun rises = ALWAYS. Rain on Tuesday = SOMETIMES. Fish in lava = NEVER. Lunch is sandwich = SOMETIMES. School has a roof = ALWAYS. A tree dances = NEVER.

parts.student_instructions: Draw or write one event that ALWAYS happens at your school.
parts.visual_layout: Big blank box for drawing/writing; sentence frame 'ALWAYS: ___'.
parts.answer_key: Many valid (e.g., 'the bell rings', 'the sun rises').

parts.student_instructions: Write or draw an event that SOMETIMES happens. Tell why it is SOMETIMES, not ALWAYS or NEVER.
parts.visual_layout: Box with prompt 'SOMETIMES event: ___'; below, sentence frame 'It is SOMETIMES because ___'.
parts.answer_key: Many valid (e.g., 'it rains' — 'because it doesn't happen every day, but it does happen sometimes').

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw one event that NEVER happens at your school.
teacher_notes: Watch for SOMETIMES catchall — children using SOMETIMES for everything they're not sure about. Drill the 'every day or no day?' test. Likelihood-language gateway to Grade 1 probability.
